age.evidence: Three-month-old C57BL/6 mice weighing approximately 25-30 g were used. Body weights [rats] were maintained at 320-350 g

sex.evidence: Male Sprague-Dawley rats and male C57BL/6 mice were obtained from Harlan Sprague-Dawley

dosing.doses_raw: training dose 5 mg/kg (5 min pretreatment); head-twitch test doses 2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg
dosing.evidence: DMT, DiPT, and DOI were dissolved in 0.9 % saline. All drugs were administered i.p. ... DMT (5 mg/kg, 5 min) ... doses of either DMT or DiPT (2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg).

dosing.doses_raw: training dose 5 mg/kg (15 min pretreatment); head-twitch test doses 2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg
dosing.evidence: DiPT (5 mg/kg, 15 min) ... doses of either DMT or DiPT (2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg).

group_housing.evidence: All rats were housed individually ... Mice ... were group housed (two to four per cage). [Mixed: rats single-housed; mice group-housed]

day_night_flipped.evidence: maintained on a 12:12 light/dark cycle (lights on at 7:00 AM)

enrichment_housing.evidence: No mention of home cage enrichment.

assays.assay_description: Two-lever operant drug discrimination in rats trained to discriminate DMT (5 mg/kg, 5 min) or DiPT (5 mg/kg, 15 min) from saline under an FR10 schedule for sucrose pellets. Test sessions lasted up to 20 min. Antagonists (MDL100907, SB242084, LY379268, LY341495) were tested for ability to attenuate or facilitate the discriminative stimulus.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered i.p. in a volume of 1 ml/kg.

setup_habituation.evidence: No separate apparatus habituation described prior to training.

setup_restrain.evidence: Rats were placed in the experimental chamber and freely responded on levers.

food_restriction.evidence: Body weights were maintained at 320-350 g by limiting food to 20 g/day, which included the food received during training sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: Water was freely available in the home cages.

time_to_assay.evidence: pretreatment time was 5 or 15 min, respectively. After the pretreatment time, the rats were placed in the experimental chamber

sample_size.evidence: The ability of MDL100907, SB242084, LY341495, and LY379268 were tested in groups of seven rats trained to discriminate DMT or DiPT from saline.

outcomes.summary: MDL100907 (5-HT2A inverse agonist) fully blocked DMT discriminative stimulus effects but only partially blocked DiPT. SB242084 (5-HT2C antagonist) partially attenuated DiPT effects with minimal effect on DMT. LY379268 (mGlu2/3 agonist) produced partial blockade of DMT but no effect on DiPT. LY341495 (mGlu2/3 antagonist) produced a leftward shift in both DMT and DiPT dose-response curves.
outcomes.evidence: MDL100907 dose-dependently blocked the effects of DMT ... LY341495 produced a dose-dependent leftward shift in both the DMT and DiPT dose-effect curves

B1_num_measures.evidence: percentage of responses on the drug-appropriate lever ... Response rates were expressed as a function of the number of responses made divided by the total session time.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data were collected until 20 food pellets were obtained or for a maximum of 20 min [single session totals].

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioral sequences or transitions.

B4_ethological.evidence: Lever pressing is not an ethological behavior.

B5_social.evidence: Rats were tested alone in operant chambers; assay does not target social cognition.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Drug discrimination is a learned operant task requiring association between drug state and lever choice.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: computers were programmed in MED-PC IV (Med Associates) for the operation of the chambers and collection of data

B8_multivariate.evidence: Response rate data were analyzed by one-way, repeated measures analysis of variance.

E2_shelter.evidence: Operant chamber provides no enclosed refuge.

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard operant chamber, no bedding reported.

E6_spatial.evidence: Standard two-lever operant chamber, single compartment.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each rat tested alone in the operant chamber.

E8_food_water.evidence: Food (45 mg sucrose pellets; Bio-Serve) was available under a fixed-ratio 10 schedule of reinforcement.

D1_continuity.evidence: A repeated-measures design was used, such that each rat was tested at all doses ... At least 3 days elapsed between test sessions.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Test sessions lasted for a maximum of 20 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Animals received approximately 60 training sessions in total before use in any behavioral experiment ... At least 3 days elapsed between test sessions.

D4_baseline.evidence: No separate pre-drug baseline recording for test assay; training data not analyzed as baseline.

D5_followup.evidence: Testing was acute, 5-15 min after drug administration; no follow-up >=24h.

D6_circadian.evidence: Test sessions lasted for a maximum of 20 min.

assays.assay_description: Mice placed in a separate holding cage (same size as home cage, 8"x10") containing clean bedding; behavior recorded for 10 min after injection of DMT, DiPT, DOI, or vehicle (with or without MDL100907 pretreatment). Head twitches counted manually by multiple observers from video.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered i.p. in a volume of 1 ml/kg.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were kept in their home cages until testing began ... placed into a separate holding cage ... where their behavior was recorded

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed into a separate holding cage and recorded while freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: Mice had ad libitum food and water access [in home cage]; no food in recording cage during the 10-min observation.

water_restriction.evidence: Mice had ad libitum food and water access [in home cage]; no water in recording cage.

time_to_assay.evidence: behavior was recorded for 10 min after the last injection of DMT or DiPT or vehicle. When DOI was tested, the animals were recorded 10 min after administration

sample_size.evidence: Groups consisted of at least seven mice.

outcomes.summary: DMT and DiPT each dose-dependently increased head twitches, with DiPT producing twofold more head twitches at 10 mg/kg (11.9±2.0) than DMT (5.4±1.8). DOI (1 mg/kg) elicited ~18 head twitches. MDL100907 (0.03 mg/kg) significantly reduced head twitches elicited by both DMT and DiPT.
outcomes.statistics: DOI: F(3,24)=21.755, p<0.001; hallucinogen F(1,115)=73.989, p<0.001; hallucinogen dose F(2,115)=188.727, p<0.001; antagonist dose F(2,115)=27.765, p<0.001; antagonist×hallucinogen F(2,115)=6.958, p=0.001; hallucinogen×dose F(2,115)=9.37, p<0.001; three-way F(4,115)=3.753, p=0.007
outcomes.evidence: DMT and DiPT each dose-dependently increased the number of head twitches (p<0.05), but DiPT produced twofold more head twitches at 10 mg/kg (11.9±2.0) than did DMT (5.4±1.8). The higher dose of MDL100907 (0.03 mg/kg) reduced head twitches elicited by 10 mg/kg of DMT and DiPT (p<0.05).

B1_num_measures.evidence: the number of head twitches were counted

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total head twitches counted over 10 min; no within-session time bins reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours in the rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Mice recorded alone in holding cage.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Head-twitch is a reflexive motor response; no learning required.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Multiple observers later viewed the recordings and the number of head twitches were counted.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Three-way ANOVA on a single behavioral metric.

E1_environment_type.evidence: placed into a separate holding cage, the same size as their home cage (8"x10")

E2_shelter.evidence: Open holding cage, no enclosed refuge.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material reported in holding cage.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice were placed individually into a separate holding cage.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in the recording cage during the 10-min observation.

D1_continuity.evidence: behavior was recorded for 10 min after the last injection

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single test session per animal/condition; no repeated days described.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline head-twitch recording reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Recording was acute (10 min post-injection); no follow-up >=24h.

D6_circadian.evidence: Each recording session lasted only 10 min.

judge_notes: Two distinct behavioural assays: drug discrimination (rats) and head-twitch response (mice). All candidates agreed on this structure.
Excluded non-behavioural assays from scoring: [125I]DOI radioligand binding and IP-1 accumulation are ex vivo/in vitro receptor assays, not behavioural.
B5 social: scored 0 (None) for drug discrimination — gptoss's score of 1 was incorrect; drug discrimination does not target a social construct.

D3 for drug discrimination: scored 3 (15+) — animals received ~60 training sessions plus multiple test sessions, all with behavioural data collected. qwen's reasoning followed; glm undercounted at 2 (8-14).
Food restriction for drug discrimination: 'before' (chronic food restriction maintained pre-test), per rubric definition — qwen and glm agreed.
Group housing scored 'no' as rats (the subjects of the drug discrimination assay) were single-housed; mice were group-housed — noted as mixed in evidence.
DOI included as a separate dosing entry since it was administered to mice as a positive control.
